summary: Bryan W. Van Norden is a scholar in philosophy and sinology. He studied at Stanford University from ~1985 to 1991 and became a professor in the Philosophy Department and Department of Chinese & Japanese at Vassar College around 1996.
Bryce Ryan was a scholar in Indology. He held academic posts at Cornell University and the University of Ceylon.

Bulcsu Siklós is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski and Charles R. Bawden, and was affiliated with SOAS University of London in 1996.

Bunga Fukui worked in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Demiéville, Max Kaltenmark, and Rolf Alfred Stein, later serving as professor at Waseda University (~1978–2004).

Bunkyo Aoki specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University and as a disciple under Kozui Otani (~1910–1914), and in 1951 succeeded Tokan Tada as a Tibetan language lecturer at the University of Tokyo.

Bunsaku Kurata was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology who studied at Aoyama Gakuin and Waseda University. He held posts at the Tokyo National Museum, the National Commission for Protection of Cultural Properties, and Nara National Museum (1975).

Bunyiu Nanjio worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology. He studied at Otani University and Oxford under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell, later holding posts at the University of Tokyo and serving as director of Otani University.

Bunzaburo Matsumoto worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy after studying at the University of Tokyo (~1890–1893). He held professorships at Rikkyo University, First Higher School, and Kyoto University, where he also served as president (1908–1915).

Burchard Brentjes was an archaeologist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under Heinz Mode (~1952–1954), later succeeding Mode in 1978 and serving on the faculty from ~1954 to 1991.
Burkhard Quessel is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Hamburg, where he was a member in 1997. He later served as a curator at the British Library (attested 2002–2012).
Burton Stein was a historian and Indologist. He held academic posts at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa from ~1966 to 1989 and at SOAS University of London from ~1989 to 1996.

Burton Watson worked in sinology and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Kyoto University, holding posts at Doshisha University, Kyoto University, Columbia University (1961), and Stanford University (~1964–1965).

Byambyn Rinchen was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the Leningrad Orient Institute (~1924–1927) and Eötvös Loránd University (1956), and held a post at the National University of Mongolia.

Byung-gon Kim is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied abroad at Rissho University (attested 2007). He held a post as professor, dean, and institute director at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

C. D. Sebastian works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Banaras Hindu University, studied under Paul Williams, Gavin D'Costa, Ashok Kumar Chatterjee, and Abhimanyu Singh, and became professor of Indian philosophy at IIT Bombay (attested 2016).

C. Kunhan Raja was an Indologist and philosopher who earned a D.Phil. at Oxford. He served as the first University Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Madras (1927) and as honorary director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre.

C. M. Naim was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of California, Berkeley from ~1957 to 1960. He held a faculty career at the University of Chicago from ~1961 to 2001, becoming Professor Emeritus.
C. Peter Bankart is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held a post at Wabash College (attested 2003) and served as a visiting researcher at Dartmouth College.

C. Pierce Salguero is a Buddhist studies and history scholar who earned degrees from the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins University. He was appointed professor at Pennsylvania State University in 2010 and also held a post at the University of Pennsylvania.
C. R. Krishnamacharlu was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Madras Christian College and Pachaiyappa's College. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India from ~1911 to 1943.
